meta.description: Detail view of a pending credit card authorization message with the option to mark transactions as fraudulent or remove the mark.
meta.process_description: The program displays the complete details of a single pending authorization request to a bank employee – including card number, amount, date/time, merchant information, authorization status (approved/declined), and reason for decline. The employee can page forward through authorization records (PF8) or return to the overview screen (PF3). A key business function is fraud reporting: using PF5, the employee can flag a transaction as fraudulent or remove an existing fraud flag – the action is processed via the program COPAUS2C and persisted in the IMS database. In case of an error, the database change is rolled back.

files.CIPAUSMY: IMS data structure for the summary of pending authorizations (Pending Authorization Summary)
files.CIPAUDTY: IMS data structure for the details of a single pending authorization (Pending Authorization Detail)
files.PSBPAUTB: IMS Program Specification Block for accessing the authorization database
files.COPAU1AO: BMS map for the detail display of the authorization message on the screen

business_rules: A transaction is considered approved if the authorization code is '00'; all other codes result in it being displayed as declined (highlighted in red).
Decline reasons are looked up from a hard-coded table with 10 entries; unknown codes are displayed as 'ERROR'.
A fraud flag is a toggle: if a transaction is already flagged as fraud (PA-FRAUD-CONFIRMED), the flag is removed; otherwise, it is reported as fraud.
Fraud actions are processed via the external program COPAUS2C; in case of an error (EIBRESP ≠ NORMAL or WS-FRD-UPDT-FAILED), the database change is fully rolled back (ROLLBACK).
The program can only be invoked if a valid account number (numeric) and a selected authorization key from the overview screen (COPAUS0C) are present.
Using PF8, the operator can navigate to the next pending authorization for the same account; at the end of the list, an appropriate informational message is displayed.
Using PF3, the operator returns to the authorization overview (COPAUS0C) without making any changes.
IMS database accesses are finalized with a Syncpoint upon completion to ensure data consistency.

variables.name: WS-REPORT-FRAUD
variables.description: Condition value: Indicates that the agent triggered the 'Report Fraud' action. If the parent action field contains the value 'F', the transaction is flagged as fraudulent in the subsequent program COPAUS2C.

variables.name: WS-REMOVE-FRAUD
variables.description: Condition value: Indicates that the agent triggered the 'Remove Fraud Flag' action. If the parent action field contains the value 'R', a previously set fraud flag on the transaction is removed in the subsequent program COPAUS2C (toggle logic).

variables.name: WS-FRD-UPDATE-STATUS
variables.description: Result status of the fraud database update performed by COPAUS2C. Indicates whether the fraud flag or its removal was successfully saved to the database or failed. In case of failure, a ROLLBACK of the entire database change is triggered.

variables.name: WS-FRD-UPDT-SUCCESS
variables.description: Condition value: Confirms that the fraud flag (or its removal) was successfully saved to the IMS database. The program can display a success message to the agent and continue normally.

variables.name: WS-FRD-UPDT-FAILED
variables.description: Condition value: Indicates that the fraud flag could not be saved to the database. Triggers a full ROLLBACK of the database changes to ensure data consistency, and causes an error message to be displayed to the agent.

variables.name: WS-FRD-ACT-MSG
variables.description: Error message text from the fraud reporting program COPAUS2C. Contains a human-readable description of the error that occurred during fraud flagging or its removal, and is displayed to the agent on screen so they can understand the error.

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-INFO
variables.description: Group field: Contains all navigation- and session-related information for displaying the Pending Authorization View Detail. Exchanged between programs COPAUS0C and COPAUS1C via the COMMAREA to maintain the current display context (selected transaction, page position, key).

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-PAU-SEL-FLG
variables.description: Selection indicator: Specifies whether the agent has actually selected a pending authorization on the summary page (COPAUS0C). Checked by program COPAUS1C before building the detail view — if no valid selection is present, processing is aborted.

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-PAU-SELECTED
variables.description: Database key of the pending authorization message selected by the agent on the summary page. Used as an IMS search key to read the complete detail record (CIPAUDTY) from the authorization database and display it on screen.

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-PAUKEY-PREV-PG
variables.description: Navigation storage for backward paging: table of up to 20 IMS database keys, each representing the first authorization of a previously visited page. Allows the agent to navigate backward page by page through the list of pending authorizations without performing a full re-scan of the data.

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-PAUKEY-LAST
variables.description: IMS database key of the last authorization displayed on the current page. Used as the starting point for the next page (PF8 navigation) to read the subsequent authorizations for the same account from the IMS database.

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: Current page number in the list of pending authorizations. Used for forward/backward page navigation and displayed to the agent on screen so they can track their navigation progress within the authorization list.

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-NEXT-PAGE-FLG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether additional pending authorizations exist for the account. Controls whether the agent can page forward to the next page using PF8. Initialized to 'N' (no further page) by default; set to 'Y' when the IMS database returns additional entries.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-YES
variables.description: Condition value: Confirms that further pending authorizations for the account exist in the database. Allows the agent to navigate to the next authorization using PF8.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-NO
variables.description: Condition value: Indicates that no further pending authorizations exist for the account. When PF8 navigation is attempted, an appropriate informational message is displayed to the agent ('End of list reached').

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-AUTH-KEYS
variables.description: Table of up to 5 IMS database keys for the pending authorizations displayed on the current summary page. Enables the agent to directly select a specific authorization on the summary page (COPAUS0C) without re-querying the database.

variables.name: CDEMO-CPVD-FRAUD-DATA
variables.description: Transfer buffer for fraud information between programs COPAUS1C and COPAUS2C. Contains the fraud-processing-relevant data of the selected transaction (e.g., transaction key, account number, action type) required by the external fraud reporting program to perform the database update.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY
variables.description: Group field (record structure): Represents the IMS record for the pending authorization summary (CIPAUSMY). Contains the summary data for multiple pending authorizations of an account as read from the IMS database to build the list view in COPAUS0C.

variables.name: PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS
variables.description: Group field (record structure): Represents the IMS record containing the full details of a single pending authorization (CIPAUDTY). Contains all fields of an authorization message (amount, merchant, authorization code, fraud status, etc.) displayed on the detail screen (COPAU1AO).

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: CICS communication area (COMMAREA): Standard structure for data exchange between CICS programs. Contains all session-relevant information (user, context, navigation state, selected authorization) passed between CardDemo programs (e.g., COPAUS0C → COPAUS1C → COPAUS2C).

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: Technical placeholder for receiving the CICS COMMAREA: defines the entry point of the passed communication data with a minimum length of 1 byte. Within the program, it is redirected (via REDEFINES or addressing) to the actual CARDDEMO-COMMAREA structure in order to access all passed session and navigation data.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central control paragraph of the program: it checks the entry context, evaluates the bank employee's keyboard input, and derives the corresponding business action (display, fraud flagging, navigation) from it.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: Loads the complete details of a selected authorization request from the IMS database, provided a valid account number and authorization key are present, and prepares the detail display for the bank employee.

paragraphs.name: MARK-AUTH-FRAUD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls the fraud reporting of a pending authorization transaction: it automatically detects whether a fraud flag should be set or removed (toggle logic), delegates the database update to the fraud program COPAUS2C, and ensures data consistency through rollback in the event of errors.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PF8-KEY
paragraphs.description: Navigates to the next pending authorization request for the same account and displays its details. If no further authorization exists, the employee is shown a corresponding notification.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-AUTH-DETAILS
paragraphs.description: Prepares all relevant details of a pending authorization request for screen display – including card data, amount, authorization status, rejection reason, merchant information, and fraud status. The paragraph is only executed if no error is present.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls the return to the authorization overview (COPAUS0C) when the employee presses PF3. The current program identity is written to the communication area before control is transferred to the overview program.

paragraphs.name: SEND-AUTHVIEW-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Prepares the detail view of a pending authorization message for screen output and displays it to the bank employee – either as a full new display (screen clear) or as an updated view.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-AUTHVIEW-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Receives the bank employee's input from the detail view of the authorization message – in particular the key commands (e.g., PF5 for fraud reporting, PF8 for scrolling forward, PF3 for return) as well as any screen fields.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Populates the header area of the detail view with application titles, transaction and program identifiers, and the current system date and time, so that the bank employee can trace the processing context and the time of the display.

paragraphs.name: READ-AUTH-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Loads the complete details of a single pending authorization request from the IMS database – first the account summary record, then the specific detail record of the selected transaction.

paragraphs.name: READ-NEXT-AUTH-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the next pending authorization record for the same account from the IMS database, in order to display the next authorization request to the employee when scrolling forward (PF8).

paragraphs.name: UPDATE-AUTH-DETAILS
paragraphs.description: Writes the updated authorization (with the fraud flag set or removed) permanently to the IMS database and confirms the result to the employee – or rolls back all changes completely in the event of a database error.

paragraphs.name: TAKE-SYNCPOINT
paragraphs.description: Commits all database changes made (e.g., setting or removing a fraud flag) definitively, thereby ensuring the permanent consistency of the authorization data in the IMS database.

paragraphs.name: ROLL-BACK
paragraphs.description: Reverses all database changes of the current transaction to maintain data consistency – called when fraud reporting or removal has failed and no inconsistent state may remain in the IMS database.

paragraphs.name: SCHEDULE-PSB
paragraphs.description: Establishes the connection to the IMS authorization database by allocating the required database access plan (PSB) – a prerequisite for reading authorization details and writing fraud flags.
